sportsdataverse.basketball.easl — 18 endpoints. Note: WARNING: UNOFFICIAL THIRD-PARTY INTERMEDIARY. These wrappers read easl.joshricha.com/api/v1, an Express server run by an individual. It is not EASL's and not Sportradar's: it mirrors Sportradar DataCore (organisation b1e0z) into SQLite and serves it keyless, and it can change or vanish without notice. Its routes, field names (steak, facebook_username) and sync freshness are the proxy author's. A first-party DataCore feed needs credentials this package does not have. The host serves no robots.txt (404) and states no terms; the runtime waits at least 1 s before every request, retries included, and honours Retry-After. Payloads are not redistributed as release assets. Note: Seasons are END years (2026 = EASL 25-26). The server's season key is the START year; easl_runtime reads the season list, maps the END year to the DataCore seasonId and defaults to the ACTIVE season. Four editions exist (2023-24 to 2026-27). The server defaults to the active season on /matches, /standings and /leaders; the runtime always sends the resolved seasonId. A season is two calendar years: group by season_id, not by the year of the tip-off. Note: Finished games only: the game routes first read the fixture and refuse (AssetFetchError) one that is not CONFIRMED with two scores, a box score whose player points do not add up to the score (the server serves one-team, four-row boxes for some games), a play-by-play that does not end on the final score in its highest period (4 or more, and the last period of the period table), and team totals that disagree with the score. For the ACTIVE season's fixture lists the runtime reads /health: a server clock more than a day from yours, or a game still SCHEDULED more than a day after its tip-off, means the mirror has stalled (AssetFetchError). That proves the mirror kept up with the games played, not that a game is final upstream. Note: Ids: every DataCore id is a UUID v1 string. team_id = entityId, player_id = personId; fixture_number (YYSSNNN) is null on every 2023-24 fixture; row_id columns are the sync server's own integers, not DataCore ids. The fixture's competitors come in arbitrary order: read home / away_*, which the parsers take from isHome. Note: No shot x/y, no game clock and no lineups exist on this server. The play-by-play text always says 'missed' for field goals and 'Free throw K of M made' for free throws, made or not: use points_scored (the change of the event team's running score), which lags on a minority of events. 301 of 2,444 sampled box rows are players who did not play (null minutes and counting stats; points are 0); player_box.played tells them apart. easl_player_stats ignores a season filter: it is the career line over every season. Names: nameFullLocal is the English display name and nameFullLatin the native-script name, so the columns are name and name_native.

build_family(league: 'str') -> 'dict[str, Any]' Return a dict of public callables for league. All callables are fully independent closures over the single league string; none share mutable state. The dict is ready to be spread into a module namespace via globals().update(...). Parameters Returns Keys are the public function names (e.g. "ahl_schedule").

echl_game_corsi(game_id: 'int', return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' Player-level on-ice Corsi and Fenwick for a single ECHL game. Parameters Returns One row per player on ice for a shot attempt: player_id (Int64), corsi_for / corsi_against / corsi_for_pct, fenwick_for / fenwick_against / fenwick_for_pct, corsi_includes_missed (Boolean), toi_seconds (Int64) and corsi_for_per60 (Float64, null without time on ice). A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_game_shifts(game_id: 'int', return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' Parsed shift stints for a single ECHL game. Parameters Returns One row per shift: game_id and player_id (Int64), first_name, last_name, jersey_number, home (Int64, 1 = home), period, start_time / end_time / length (clock strings), start_s / end_s (Int64 seconds) and the goal_on_shift / penalty_on_shift flags. A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_game_summary(game_id: 'int') -> 'dict' ECHL game summary — dict of frames (game/goals/penalties/shots_by_period/three_stars). Parameters Returns game (one row: game_id, date, status, venue, attendance, both teams and scores), goals (one row per goal with the scorer, both assists and the plus / minus skaters), penalties (one row per penalty), shots_by_period (side, period, shots) and three_stars. When the league denies the summary view, the event frames are empty and game is a game_id stub row. Raises

echl_leaders(season: 'Optional[int]' = None, season_id: 'Optional[int]' = None, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' ECHL statistical leaders for a given season. Parameters Returns One row per ranked skater (points and goals leaders): rank (Int64), player_id, name, jersey_number, position, team_id / team_name / team_code, stat_formatted and type_formatted (player_id / team_id Int64, the rest String), plus photo and logo URLs. A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_pbp(game_id: 'int', return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' ECHL play-by-play — one row per event, fully enriched. Parameters Returns One row per event (shot, goal, penalty, faceoff, hit, goalie change ...): game_id, event, team_id, period_of_game, time_of_period, rink x_coord / y_coord (Float64, feet, centre ice at (0, 0); the raw 600×300 feed canvas values are x_coord_original / y_coord_original), the feet frames x_coord_fixed / y_coord_fixed (home team shoots right) and x_coord_right / y_coord_right (every team shoots right), the primary / second / third player and goalie ids (Int64) and names, the plus / minus skaters on a goal, game metadata from the game summary, and derived shot_distance / shot_angle / scoring_chance and the on_ice_home / on_ice_away skaters from the shift feed. Some leagues (USHL, MJHL) publish only goals, penalties and goalie changes, with no coordinates. A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_player_stats(player_id: 'int', return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' ECHL player season stats across all seasons. Parameters Returns One row per season (and team) the player played: season_id, season_name, playoff, team_id / team_name / team_code, games_played, goals, assists, points, plus_minus, penalty_minutes, power-play / short-handed / shootout splits, shots, faceoff_wins / faceoff_attempts, ice_time and stat_type. season_id and team_id are Int64; the rest are String, as the feed ships them. A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_player_toi(game_id: 'int', return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' Per-player time-on-ice totals for a single ECHL game. Parameters Returns One row per player: player_id (Int64), first_name, last_name, toi_seconds (Int64), num_shifts and avg_shift_s (Float64). A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_schedule(season: 'Optional[int]' = None, season_id: 'Optional[int]' = None, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' ECHL schedule — one row per game of one season. Parameters Returns One row per game: game_id, game_date, game_status, home_team / home_team_id / home_score, away_team / away_team_id / away_score, venue, season_id and game_type; the *_id columns are Int64, the rest String. Only the requested season's games: a regular season, its playoffs and its preseason are separate season ids, so pass season_id (from echl_season_id()) for the playoffs. A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_standings(season: 'Optional[int]' = None, season_id: 'Optional[int]' = None, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' ECHL standings — one row per team. Parameters Returns One row per team: team, team_code, team_rank and wins (Int64), and games_played, losses, regulation_wins, non_reg_wins, non_reg_losses, points, goals_for, goals_against, games_remaining, percentage and overall_rank (String, as the feed ships them). A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_team_roster(team_id: 'int', season: 'Optional[int]' = None, season_id: 'Optional[int]' = None, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' ECHL team roster for a given team + season. Parameters Returns One row per rostered player: player_id, person_id, names (first_name, last_name, display_name), position, tp_jersey_number, shoots / catches, height / weight, birthdate, home and birth places, rookie, veteran_status, draft_status and player_image. The id / *_id columns are Int64; the rest are String, as the feed ships them. A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_teams(season: 'Optional[int]' = None, season_id: 'Optional[int]' = None, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' ECHL teams for a given season. Parameters Returns One row per team: team_id, team_name, team_code, team_nickname, team_label, division and team_logo; team_id is Int64, the rest String. A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

echl_season_id(return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False) -> 'Any' All ECHL seasons with end-year + game-type labels. A pandas DataFrame when return_as_pandas is True. Raises

most_recent_echl_season() -> 'int' Newest ECHL regular season as an end-year integer: the highest season_yr of a regular season that is not a one-off event, so a preseason listed first is not a default. Returns The newest regular season's END year (2026 = the 2025-26 season). Raises

sportsdataverse-py is the Python member of the SportsDataverse — a family of free, open-source packages that put clean, tidy sports data in the hands of analysts across R, Python, and Node.js. This page explains the design philosophy the package shares with its sister projects, the function-naming paradigm that makes the surface predictable, and how to move between the Python and R packages (and the wider open-source sports ecosystem) without relearning anything.

Four ideas run through every SportsDataverse package: Free and open. The data is public; the tooling that tidies it should be too. Everything here is MIT-licensed and community-maintained. Tidy by default. Raw sports APIs return deeply-nested JSON. The job of a SportsDataverse package is to flatten that into rectangular, analysis-ready tables — polars/pandas DataFrames here, tibbles in R — with stable column names you can build a model on. One mental model across sports and languages. Learn the pattern once and it transfers: the same verbs (scoreboard, pbp, team_roster, player_gamelog, load_*) mean the same thing in nba and wnba and cfb, and the name you call in Python is the name you'd call in the R sister package. Benchmarkable models. Beyond aggregation, the project exists to make open-source expected-points (EP) and win-probability (WP) work — especially for American football — reproducible and comparable.

Once you know the prefixes, you can usually guess the function name. Two conventions keep the ESPN surface aligned with the R packages: R-aligned vocabulary. ESPN's raw taxonomy is normalized to the cfbfastR/hoopR/wehoop wording: an athlete is a player, an event is a game, a competitor is a game team. So you call espn_nba_player_overview() (not athlete_overview) and espn_cfb_game_plays() (not event_plays) — across every league. Collision resolution (one bare name). When two endpoints would resolve to the same name, one keeps the clean bare name and the other is version-qualified. Every league therefore has a bare espn_<league>_player_stats() (season stats) alongside the comprehensive espn_<league>_player_stats_v3(). Return types are predictable: parser-backed wrappers return a polars DataFrame by default — pass return_parsed=False for the raw Dict; wrappers without a parser return the Dict. Use return_as_pandas=True to get a pandas DataFrame. (The old sportsdataverse.parsed.<league> mirror is deprecated: import from sportsdataverse.<league> instead.) See Architecture and Parsers for the full story.

The load_<league>_*() functions skip live scraping entirely — they read pre-built, season-partitioned parquet that the SportsDataverse data pipelines publish on a schedule, and they are 404-safe (a season with no published asset is skipped with a warning rather than raising). The data comes from a small set of release hosts: sportsdataverse-data — the GitHub Releases host that almost every load_* function reads from (NBA, WNBA, MBB, WBB, CFB, NHL, PWHL, MLB, …). nflverse-data — NFL data, read through the nflreadpy-style nfl module. The releases are built by per-league producer repositories, for example hoopR-nba-data, wehoop-wnba-data, cfbfastR-cfb-data, fastRhockey-nhl-data, fastRhockey-pwhl-data and baseballr-data. The R packages read the same releases, so a loader returns the same data in both languages.

Each generated-loader league's Loaders reference page carries an Automation status table mapping every dataset to its release tag and the pipeline that produces it, so you can see at a glance what's current and where it comes from: NBA loaders · WNBA loaders · MBB loaders · WBB loaders CFB loaders · NHL loaders · PWHL loaders NFL loaders (nflverse and SDV-native releases) · MLB loaders

sdv-py deliberately mirrors the R packages' names, so a call you know in R is the call you make in Python. The leagues below have an R sister; the rest of the registry (international basketball, European and junior hockey, soccer, cricket, the cross-sport providers) is Python-only for now. Each sport's R sister: For example, today's WNBA scoreboard is the same verb in both languages: # R (wehoop) wehoop::espn_wnba_scoreboard() # Python (sportsdataverse-py) from sportsdataverse.wnba import espn_wnba_scoreboard espn_wnba_scoreboard(return_parsed=True)

A representative slice of the surface — each sportsdataverse-py function links to its reference page, and each R function links to its sister-package docs. The pattern holds well beyond these rows: ESPN wrappers, native league APIs, and load_* release loaders all line up. Where they diverge: sdv-py exposes one function per ESPN surface (espn_nba_teams_site vs espn_nba_season_teams) where the R packages often collapse them into a single function with branching internals; and sdv-py returns polars by default rather than a data.frame/tibble. Beyond the sport packages, the SportsDataverse spans languages and utilities: R umbrella & utilities — sportsdataverse-R (the meta-package that loads them all), oddsapiR (betting odds), recruitR (recruiting), cfbseedR (college football season simulation and CFP seeding), sportyR (field/court/rink plots), and sdvplotR (team logos, wordmarks, headshots and colors for ggplot2, gt and reactable). Python siblings — sdvplot (team logos, wordmarks, headshots and colors for Python plots and tables), sportypy (the Python port of sportyR) and collegebaseball. Node.js — sportsdataverse.js and sdvplot-js (@sportsdataverse/sdvplot, @sportsdataverse/sporty and @sportsdataverse/sdvtables). The full directory is at sportsdataverse.org/packages.

SportsDataverse builds on and complements two neighboring communities: nflverse — the NFL-focused open ecosystem (nflfastR and nflreadr in R, nflreadpy in Python). The sportsdataverse.nfl module mirrors nflreadpy's load_* surface and reads the same nflverse parquet releases, so nflverse users can swap engines with minimal changes. PySport — the open-source sports-analytics community and its curated directory of Python libraries. sdv-py sits alongside league-specific tools you may already use — nba_api, pybaseball, and nhl-api-py — and is happy to be one tidy layer in a larger toolbox rather than the only one.

f1_laps(season: 'str', round: 'str', *, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False, **kwargs: 'Any') -> 'Union[pl.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]' Lap times of one race: one row per driver per lap (1996+), all pages. Endpoint: GET https://api.jolpi.ca/ergast/f1/{season}/{round}/laps.json, requested with limit=100 and offset advanced page by page until MRData.total timings have been read. Parameters Returns A polars/pandas DataFrame with the laps_page columns (season, round, race_*, lap_number, driver_id, position, time), concatenated across pages; zero rows (same columns) when the race has no lap data (before 1996, or a round not yet run). Raises Example from sportsdataverse.f1 import f1_laps df = f1_laps(2024, 1) print(df.shape) # (1129, 17) -- 12 requests # Pipeline next step (one line) import polars as pl df.filter(pl.col("driver_id") == "max_verstappen").select("lap_number", "position", "time")

sportsdataverse.f1 — 15 endpoints. Note: Data license CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, attribution, share-alike): sdv-py wraps the API on the caller's behalf and never republishes Jolpica payloads as release assets. Note: Rate limit 4 requests/second burst, 500 requests/hour sustained, unauthenticated, per IP and shared by every process on the machine. Paging: limit is capped at 100 (a larger value is clamped and echoed in MRData.limit); offset pages the innermost rows counted by MRData.total. Note: season accepts current; round accepts last / next. Paths are case-insensitive.

sportsdataverse.basketball.feb — 11 endpoints. Note: Legal notice: the FEB's aviso legal asserts intellectual-property rights over the site's content and databases (the EU database right). It has no explicit scraping clause and robots.txt returns 404 on both hosts, but SportsDataverse has not ruled on it: fetching on your own machine is fine; a published data release or a hosted mirror needs a legal sign-off first. Note: Unofficial and unsupported: the LiveStats API is the federation's own widget backend, not a documented public API. It needs a bearer JWT, which is public: feb_runtime reads it from the site's home page at run time, keeps it in memory for the process (24 h validity) and never prints, logs or writes it. Note: Coverage: the game routes answer from 2020-21 (Liga Femenina Endesa from its first game; Primera FEB from 2021-03-12, so its earlier 2020-21 games answer 404, as do all earlier seasons). 2020-21 play-by-play is text only. The schedule pages go back to 1996-97 (season=1997). Segunda FEB and the youth and Tercera FEB groups share the same routes; group is the site's menu group (1 Primera FEB, 2 Segunda FEB, 4 Liga Femenina Endesa). Note: Seasons are END years everywhere in this package (season=2027 is 2026-27); the site's own t is the START year, so the runtime sends t = season - 1 (t=2026 is 2026-27).

documents.t: fiba_afrobasket_editions(season: 'Optional[int]' = None, to_season: 'Optional[int]' = None, *, return_parsed: 'bool' = True, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False, **kwargs: 'Any') -> 'Union[pl.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, Dict]' Every edition of FIBA AfroBasket. FIBA AfroBasket (men's); season rule: event year (2025 = 2025). Convenience wrapper: a thin binding of fiba_gdap_editions to this competition, minted from the competition registry (tools/codegen/basketball_competitions.yaml). Read before use: FIBA's terms restrict this source. The GDAP developer-portal terms limit API use to 'Authorized Users' (federations, organisers, FIBA partners) and say any broader use 'is not authorised'; the fiba.basketball terms say no portion of the site may be duplicated, redistributed or manipulated. The package owner reviewed both clauses on 2026-10-12, accepted them and approved the full intake, published data releases included. Note: Id key spaces: competition_id is one per edition (2023 World Cup = 208182) and game_id is global across competitions (the of a game-page URL). team_id is per team per competition (Germany is 279569 at the 2023 World Cup and 281545 at Paris 2024), while organisation_id is the stable federation or club (64 = Germany, every year); the game page's T_ and the play-by-play oId are organisation ids, not team ids. Note: The wrapper takes the game id and its competition (comp) and builds the real page URL from GDAP (the competition's marketing name gives the history slug, its schedule gives the two team codes; a competition with an event page is tried at its event URL when the archive URL answers the not-found shell, and the Champions League host last). The 'Example URL' above is the wrapper's route, not a page FIBA serves. Note: Box scores start about 2006; play-by-play with shot x/y about 2012 (OVR events) and 2017-18 (FLS club competitions). A game with no box score raises NoDataError; a game still live raises AssetFetchError. fiba.basketball answers plain requests with HTTP 403, so the page transport is curl_cffi with Chrome TLS (extra: pip install sportsdataverse[all]). Shot x/y are image pixels with an unverified scale.

sportsdataverse.basketball.fiba_hub — 31 endpoints. Note: FIBA's terms restrict this source. The GDAP developer-portal terms limit API use to 'Authorized Users' (federations, organisers, FIBA partners) and say any broader use 'is not authorised'; the fiba.basketball terms say no portion of the site may be duplicated, redistributed or manipulated. The package owner reviewed both clauses on 2026-10-12, accepted them and approved the full intake, published data releases included. Users who are not themselves authorised by FIBA should check the terms before using the wrappers. Note: The GDAP subscription key is public (fiba.basketball ships it in every page); the runtime reads it from the live page at run time and never logs it. Officials' contact details and coaches' and officials' dates of birth are dropped from every body. Additional functions in sportsdataverse.basketball.genius that are not generated API-endpoint wrappers (those have their own reference pages): per-competition functions minted from the competition registry (each binds a base wrapper to one competition), plus hand-written wrappers, loaders, and helpers.

documents.t: bal_competitions(*, return_parsed: 'bool' = True, return_as_pandas: 'bool' = False, **kwargs: 'Any') -> 'Union[pl.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, Dict]' Every competition of the BAL Genius org, with its END-year season. Basketball Africa League (men's); season rule: calendar year (BAL 2025 = 2025); 2023 lists two competitions, so pass comp_id. Convenience wrapper: a thin binding of genius_competitions to this competition, minted from the competition registry (tools/codegen/basketball_competitions.yaml). Read before use: Access: the Genius hosts publish no robots.txt and no terms. CloudFront refuses datacenter IPs on the LiveStats and hosted hosts: from a server set the optional GENIUS_PROXY environment variable to an http(s) proxy URL (it is never logged or printed). The wrappers space requests at least one second apart and read only the Genius hosts; keep crawls slow and incremental. Some league sites (the NZ NBL) forbid AI crawlers in their own robots.txt, which does not cover these hosts. Parameters Returns A polars/pandas DataFrame by default; the chooser page record (dict) plus _request (the org asked for) when return_parsed=False. Raises Example from sportsdataverse.basketball.genius import bal_competitions bal_competitions()

sportsdataverse.basketball.genius — 11 endpoints. Note: Access: the Genius hosts publish no robots.txt and no terms. CloudFront refuses datacenter IPs on the LiveStats and hosted hosts: from a server set the optional GENIUS_PROXY environment variable to an http(s) proxy URL (it is never logged or printed). The wrappers space requests at least one second apart and read only the Genius hosts; keep crawls slow and incremental. Some league sites (the NZ NBL) forbid AI crawlers in their own robots.txt, which does not cover these hosts. Note: Org and season. Every competition is an ORG code plus a competition id (comp_id): genius_competitions lists an org's competitions with the sdv END-year season (a START-year org lists 2025-26 as season 2026), genius_match_competition maps a game to its competition, and data.json itself names no date, competition or season. The hosted ORG can differ from the LiveStats ORG of /u/ (NZNBL vs NZN). Match ids are one global sequence across every Genius customer. Note: data.json carries no global team or player id: tno (1 or 2) and pno are in-game numbers. Join players across games on name, team code and shirt number; global team ids come from the hosted schedule, the widget or genius_competition_games. Only finished games are read.

build_family(league: 'str') -> 'dict[str, Any]' Return a dict of public callables for league. All callables are fully independent closures over the single league string; none share mutable state. The dict is ready to be spread into a module namespace via globals().update(...). Parameters Returns Keys are the public function names (e.g. "ahl_schedule").

Parameters Returns game (one row: game_id, date, status, venue, attendance, both teams and scores), goals (one row per goal with the scorer, both assists and the plus / minus skaters), penalties (one row per penalty), shots_by_period (side, period, shots) and three_stars. When the league denies the summary view, the event frames are empty and game is a game_id stub row. Raises
